request: Analyze GSE180877 for PMID 34870208 (Nucleus Type-Specific DNA Methylomics Reveals Epigenetic "Memory" of Prior Adaptation in Skeletal Muscle.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

other_accessions_not_analyzed.GSE180433: RRBS methylation (nucleus-sorted); not gene expression, outside this request

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq of whole plantaris muscle, male HSA-GFP mice (S2.5.p1, S4.p2, S4.p3)

group: 9M PoW+DT (8 wk PoWeR + 12 wk detraining, 9 mo)

final.sample_inclusion: biological triplicate per group (S4.p2); RNA-seq on the same muscles used for RRBS (S2.5.p1)
final.primary_estimand: effect of 8 wk PoWeR training on whole-muscle gene expression vs age-matched untrained (6M PoW vs 6M UT)
planned_contrasts: 6M PoW vs 6M UT (S2.5.p1; paper: 179 up + 118 down = 297 DEGs at FDR < 0.05)
9M PoW+DT vs 9M UT (S2.5.p1; paper: no PoWeR-altered gene remained DE after detraining; total count not reported)
final.normalization: Partek Flow: STAR mm10, gene counts, genes with max count <= 50 removed, median-ratio normalization (S4.p3; GEO data_processing)
final.paper_method: DESeq/DESeq2 in Partek Flow with FDR step-up (S4.p3; GEO data_processing)

6M PoW vs 6M UT.enrichment: ECM-related processes up, SMAD signaling genes down (Figure S2)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: DA.p1 names GSE180877 as the RNA-seq deposit. S2.5.p1 gives the PoWeR transcriptome result (179 up / 118 down, FDR<0.05) and the detraining persistence check. S4.p3 states Partek, min read cutoff 50, mm10, DESeq with FDR step-up. S4.1.p1 controls FDR<0.05 for all sequencing; no fold-change rule. S4.p2 says biological triplicate per group.

checks: series title equals the paper title
single supplementary matrix GSE180877_Raw_gene_counts_matrix.txt.gz covers all 15 GSMs

ownership.reasoning: Series is linked to the PMID and named in the data availability statement; the matrix column names follow the paper's group labels (6M UT, 6M PoW, 9M UT, 9M PoW+DT).

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns ('6M UT 1', '9M PoW+DT 1', '6M PoW 4') equal the GEO title prefix before the bracketed mouse ID ('6M UT1 [PoW3]', '9M PoW+DT1 [DT6]', '6M POW4 [LD1]') after ignoring case and spaces; key derived from title, exact normalized match, no positional alignment. Group labels come from the title, which agrees with the matrix headers and the paper's group names. characteristics_ch1.1.treatment is unreliable: it labels 9M UT 'Detrained' and 9M PoW+DT 'Sedentary' (swapped), and 6M POW4-6 'Sedentary'. The three later-deposited samples 6M POW4-6 [LD1-3] (Sep 03 2021) are PoW by title and by matrix header ('6M PoW 4-6'), and trained-like on ECM markers (Col3a1 CPM 72/103/81 vs UT 25/44/48), so grp pools them into PoW6 (n=6). grpx keeps them as LD6 for a triplicate-only sensitivity run.

candidates.reason_rejected: contradicts title and matrix headers for all 9M samples and for 6M POW4-6

title + matrix header both say PoW; S4.p2 triplicate statement describes the RRBS mice; first attempt (see _previous) showed the 6-vs-3 fit reproduces the paper's 179/118 almost exactly (180/118) while 3-vs-3 gives 61/34, so the paper's RNA-seq used n=6 PoW. Kept as sensitivity.

matrix.matrix_type: estimated counts (Partek Flow gene-level quantification; non-integer values)
matrix.reasoning: GEO data_processing: STAR to mm10, 'quantified for gene counts', median-ratio normalized and tested with DESeq2; supplementary file described as raw gene counts. Profile: 71% integers, values like 11.0147 and 2.56E-07 (EM-style fractional assignment), column sums 19-28 M reads, max 2.1e6, no negatives - count scale, not FPKM/TPM. The paper's input is the same count matrix (S4.p3). Rounding to integers for DESeq2 is the standard treatment of estimated counts.

design.reasoning: S2.p1/S2.5.p1: each trained group is compared with its age-matched untrained control (6M PoW vs 6M UT; 9M PoW+DT vs 9M UT). Cross-age comparisons are not sensible estimands and are not run. 6M PoW arm = 6 mice (PoW1-3 + POW4-6 [LD]) by title/matrix header; 6M UT, 9M UT, 9M PoW+DT = 3 each. Re-decided after attempt 1: the triplicate-only primary gave 64/55 (joint) and 61/34 (pair) vs paper 179/118, the pooled run gave 180/118; this, plus the label evidence, identifies the paper's sample set. Estimand is causal (training vs untrained age-matched mice).

candidates.reason_rejected: does not match the paper's sample set; run as sensitivity

candidates.value: 2x2 factorial age x training with interaction
candidates.reason_rejected: detrained is not the same treatment as trained; the paper only asks age-matched contrasts

covariance.reasoning: Independent mice, one muscle each; no repeated measures; all male. The only recorded batch-like variable is the deposit date: the 3 LD mice (Sep 2021 deposit) all sit in the PoW6 arm together with 3 Jul-deposit PoW mice, so deposit is not aliased with treatment, but it may mark a sequencing batch inside the PoW arm. A deposit term would be estimated only from within the PoW arm and the paper adjusts for nothing, so it is not added; the triplicate-only fit is run as sensitivity instead. Age is handled by within-age contrasts.

final.method: DESeq2 (pydeseq2 Wald) on rounded estimated counts, two-arm fit per age-matched contrast

paper_route.method: DESeq2 in Partek Flow, genes with max count <= 50 removed, median-ratio normalization, FDR step-up

deviations: pydeseq2 instead of Partek Flow's DESeq2 implementation
fractional estimated counts rounded to integers before DESeq2
low-count filter 'max count > 50' applied within each execution's samples
Partek model scope not stated; two-arm fits are primary (they match the paper's counts), a single 5-sample-group model is run as sensitivity

method.reasoning: Matrix supports the paper's count route. Filter reproduces GEO data_processing 'maximum count of less than or equal to 50' excluded (implemented as count >= 50.0001 in at least 1 sample, i.e. max > 50, on unrounded values).

threshold.reasoning: S2.5.p1 and S4.1.p1: FDR (BH-adjusted p) < 0.05, no fold-change rule. Audit rule adds |FC| > 1.5 (log2 0.5849625) for reference only.

caveats: GEO characteristics 'treatment' is inconsistent with titles/matrix headers; groups taken from titles

6M PoW arm includes 3 later-deposited mice (POW4-6 [LD]); the paper's 'biological triplicate per group' (S4.p2) does not hold for its RNA-seq PoW arm; the sample-set decision was revised after the first attempt
paper gives no total DEG count for 9M PoW+DT vs 9M UT; its claim is only that no PoWeR-altered gene stayed DE

Persistence check: of our 298 PoWeR DEGs, one (Dusp7) is also DE in 9M PoW+DT vs 9M UT (FDR<0.05) but with opposite sign (log2FC -0.64 trained, +0.91 detrained), so no change persists in the same direction; strictly, the paper's 'no genes altered by PoWeR remained differentially expressed' has this one opposite-sign exception in our fit.

study.reasoning: Primary reproduces the paper's estimand, sample set (as identified from labels and counts), method family and threshold; differences are implementation-level.
